result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), while lookups use `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against a URI-parsed host. Values like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (which old site settings allowed) are not normalized in the migration — the before_validation stripping only applies to model saves, and the migration uses raw SQL. So those hosts would never match after upgrade. Mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies legacy SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts lines into the new embeddable_hosts table via raw SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` (line ~24). This bypasses the EmbeddableHost model’s `before_validation` normalizer (which strips protocol and paths) because no model save/callback runs. The new matching logic in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host/host_allowed? parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, i.e., it expects rows to contain just the hostname. So legacy entries like `https://example.com/1234` or `http://discourse.org` will be stored verbatim and will not match `uri.host` after upgrade, breaking embedding for those hosts.
